Thanks so much for writing — that's a great question. Using apps and offline maps takes the guesswork out of accessible tram travel and helps you stretch your budget. First, download a reliable transit app like Citymapper or Moovit and the official transit authority app if there is one; enable the wheelchair-accessible routing option in settings so your suggested routes favor low-platform boarding and step-free transfers. Save key stops and routes offline by exporting them to your phone's offline maps or taking screenshots, because Wi‑Fi and data can be spotty when you're out and about.

Next, bookmark where to buy tickets — many systems sell tickets via app, kiosks, or local shops. Pro tip: if the app sells day passes for around €6 (≈$6.60), grab that for heavy travel days rather than paying multiple single fares at about €2.50 (≈$2.75). Validate your ticket in-app or at the validator on boarding; inspectors will want to see either a timestamped digital ticket or a stamped paper one.

Finally, practice one or two test trips close to your lodging so you learn the boarding flow and how drivers announce stops in that city. If you want, send me the city name and two addresses and I’ll map out an accessible, app-friendly route and note which stops to save offline and where to buy and validate the cheapest tickets. Happy to map a route for you.

Warmly,
Maya
